title: Deactivate controllers when hardware component is inactive

fault_phenomenon.title: Deactivate controllers when hardware component is inactive
fault_phenomenon.description:
**Describe the bug**

Following this https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/pull/1666#issuecomment-3044384471. After https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/pull/2334 the controller should be deactivated if the hardware component it depends on becomes inactive. There are few issues with current implementation:
1. The controller is only deactivated if the hardware component returns `return_type::DEACTIVATE` in write method. If deactivating using CLI the the controller stays active.
2. This probably depends on above, but It is possible to activate the controller even if the hardware component is still in INACTIVE state.
3. Only the controller that has claimed hardware interfaces is being deactivated. Other controllers that are chained are still active. All preeceding controllers should be also deactivated. If you try to deactivate the controller that is chained using CLI it will throw the following error:
  ```
  [WARN] [1751882846.567267619] [controller_manager]: Unable to deactivate controller with name 'drive_controller' because preceding controller with name 'velocity_input_controller' is currently active and will not be deactivated.
  [WARN] [1751882846.567294092] [controller_manager]: Could not deactivate controller with name 'drive_controller'. Check above warnings for more details. Check the state of the controllers and their required interfaces using `ros2 control list_controllers -v` CLI to get more information.
  [ERROR] [1751882846.567311243] [controller_manager]: Aborting, no controller is switched! (::STRICT switch)
  ```
4. Right now to resolve the inactive state you have to activate the hardware component and then activate the controller. It would be nice if this could be automated. The implementation details are open for discussion, here are a few possible approaches:
	- Allow to define a "system group" that defines all dependent hardware components and controllers. Then you could call activate on a group and manager would attempt to activate all hardware components and controllers.
	-  When calling activate on the controller also try to activate hardware component it depends on. 
	- Allow auto reactivation of controller if hardware becomes active again. 

Tested on ROS 2 Jazzy

Sure

> Can we can close this issue now that users can choose which behavior they would like at run time?

Do you mean the `defaults.allow_controller_activation_with_inactive_hardware` and `defaults.deactivate_controllers_on_hardware_self_deactivate` parameters?

It seems to me like those don't fully address this Issue. I'm running ros2_control on `jazzy` with default parameters (i.e. `allow_controller_activation_with_inactive_hardware = false` and `deactivate_controllers_on_hardware_self_deactivate = true`, and observe the following:

When I manually deactivate a HardwareComponent (`ros2 control set_hardware_component_state r6bot inactive`), 
* Any controllers using that component's interfaces **stay active**
* Consequently the interfaces **stay claimed**

When I manually de-activate the *Controller*, I can then no longer re-activate it (this is as expected).

Is there a reason to leave the controller active if a HardwareComponent becomes inactive due to a user command, rather than because it returned `return_type::DEACTIVATE` from one of its methods?

title: unable to require state interfaces exported by chainable controller

fault_phenomenon.title: unable to require state interfaces exported by chainable controller
fault_phenomenon.description:
**Describe the bug**
I have a `controller_interface::ChainableControllerInterface` that basically processes/fuses IMU data and thus only needs to import and export state interfaces.

Essentially, it is a `controller_interface::ChainableControllerInterface` that requires the state interfaces:
```C++
controller_interface::InterfaceConfiguration state_interface_configuration() const override
  {
    std::vector<std::string> interface_names = {
      //
      sensor_name + "/angular_velocity.x",
      sensor_name + "/angular_velocity.y",
      sensor_name + "/angular_velocity.z",
      //
      sensor_name + "/linear_acceleration.x",
      sensor_name + "/linear_acceleration.y",
      sensor_name + "/linear_acceleration.z",
    };
    if (use_magnetometer)
    {
      interface_names.push_back(sensor_name + "/magnetic_field.x");
      interface_names.push_back(sensor_name + "/magnetic_field.y");
      interface_names.push_back(sensor_name + "/magnetic_field.z");
    }
    return {controller_interface::interface_configuration_type::INDIVIDUAL, interface_names};
  }
```
and exports the state interfaces:
```C++
std::vector<hardware_interface::StateInterface> on_export_state_interfaces() override
  {
    std::vector<hardware_interface::StateInterface> state_interfaces;

    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/angular_velocity.x", &angular_velocity.x()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/angular_velocity.y", &angular_velocity.y()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/angular_velocity.z", &angular_velocity.z()));

    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/linear_acceleration.x", &linear_acceleration.x()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/linear_acceleration.y", &linear_acceleration.y()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/linear_acceleration.z", &linear_acceleration.z()));

    if (use_magnetometer)
    {
      state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
        get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/magnetic_field.x", &magnetic_field->x()));
      state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
        get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/magnetic_field.y", &magnetic_field->y()));
      state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
        get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/magnetic_field.z", &magnetic_field->z()));
    }

    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.w", &q_wi.w()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.x", &q_wi.x()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.y", &q_wi.y()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.z", &q_wi.z()));
    return state_interfaces;
  }
```

This works as expected. `ros2 control list_controllers -v` will show the correct state interfaces:
```
	update_rate: 500 Hz
	is_async: False
	claimed interfaces:
	required command interfaces:
	required state interfaces:
		base_imu/angular_velocity.x
		base_imu/angular_velocity.y
		base_imu/angular_velocity.z
		base_imu/linear_acceleration.x
		base_imu/linear_acceleration.y
		base_imu/linear_acceleration.z
		base_imu/magnetic_field.x
		base_imu/magnetic_field.y
		base_imu/magnetic_field.z
	chained to interfaces:
	exported reference interfaces:
	exported state interfaces:
		fusion/angular_velocity.x
		fusion/angular_velocity.y
		fusion/angular_velocity.z
		fusion/linear_acceleration.x
		fusion/linear_acceleration.y
		fusion/linear_acceleration.z
		fusion/magnetic_field.x
		fusion/magnetic_field.y
		fusion/magnetic_field.z
		fusion/orientation.w
		fusion/orientation.x
		fusion/orientation.y
		fusion/orientation.z
```

However, using this with an `imu_sensor_broadcaster/IMUSensorBroadcaster` and `sensor_name: fusion` fails with:
```
Unable to activate controller 'fusion_sensor_broadcaster' since the state interface 'fusion/orientation.x' is not available.
```
although it is clearly visible that the `required state interfaces` strings match the `exported state interfaces` above:
```
fusion_sensor_broadcaster imu_sensor_broadcaster/IMUSensorBroadcaster  inactive
	update_rate: 500 Hz
	is_async: False
	claimed interfaces:
	required command interfaces:
	required state interfaces:
		fusion/orientation.x
		fusion/orientation.y
		fusion/orientation.z
		fusion/orientation.w
		fusion/angular_velocity.x
		fusion/angular_velocity.y
		fusion/angular_velocity.z
		fusion/linear_acceleration.x
		fusion/linear_acceleration.y
		fusion/linear_acceleration.z
	chained to interfaces:
	exported reference interfaces:
	exported state interfaces:
```

The same `IMUSensorBroadcaster` works when I specify the namespace of a "real" IMU (`hardware_interface::SensorInterface`).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. create a `ChainableControllerInterface` with only state interface export/imports
2. try to import the state interfaces from another controller

**Expected behavior**
A controller should be able to require state interfaces of another chainable controller.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu
 - Version jazzy

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here, especially include any modifications to ros2_control that relate to this issue.

comments.body:
Hello!

The sensor name needs to be the name of the exporting controller + /fusion. Then it should find it. 

All exported interfaces are prepended with the name of their exporting controller.

> All exported interfaces are prepended with the name of their exporting controller.

You are right. If I export the state interfaces of a controller that I configure with name `fusion` like:
```C++
state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(get_name(), "angular_velocity.x", &angular_velocity.x()));
```
and configure the `IMUSensorBroadcaster` with `sensor_name: fusion`, it indeed does not complain anymore. 

But this is somehow not visible in the `exported state interfaces`. I.e., whatever prefix I chose for `StateInterface`, it does not show in the name of the exported state. Now, the overview looks like:
```
fusion                    uav/fusion/FusionMadgwick                    active
	required state interfaces:
		base_imu/angular_velocity.x

fusion_sensor_broadcaster imu_sensor_broadcaster/IMUSensorBroadcaster  active
	required state interfaces:
		fusion/angular_velocity.x
````

I guess you just have to know that state interfaces are automatically prefixed with the controller name. I expected this to work like the ROS topics where you would see matching topics. Maybe it would help to show these automatically prefixed state interfaces like the private topics (`~/`).
Sure, we can add that while displaying. Thanks for the input
You should see the appropriate interfaces when you run `ros2 control list_hardware_interfaces`

> You should see the appropriate interfaces when you run `ros2 control list_hardware_interfaces`

Right. I never noticed that this also lists the controller interfaces and not just the hardware interfaces. I guess, in the end, this issue is just a UI issue.
Yess!

title: configure_controller error path causes controller manager to hang for invalid chainable controllers

fault_phenomenon.title: configure_controller error path causes controller manager to hang for invalid chainable controllers
fault_phenomenon.description:
**Describe the bug**
When configuring a chainable controller that does not export any state or reference interfaces, configure_controller() returns ERROR as expected, but the controller manager does not terminate cleanly and remains active, causing tests or processes to hang indefinitely.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create a chainable controller that exports no state or reference interfaces
2. Add it to the controller manager
3. Initialize the resource manager
4. Call configure_controller
5. Observe that ERROR is returned and logged correctly, however the process/test does not terminate and hangs unless interrupted

Example:
```
// Minimal reproduction (adapted from existing test patterns)
auto bad_controller =
  std::make_shared<test_chainable_controller::TestChainableController>();

cm_->add_controller(
  bad_controller,
  "bad_chainable_controller",
  test_chainable_controller::TEST_CONTROLLER_CLASS_NAME);

pass_robot_description_to_cm_and_rm();

auto ret = cm_->configure_controller("bad_chainable_controller");
```
Expected: ERROR
Actual: returns ERROR but system does not terminate cleanly

**Expected behavior**
After returning ERROR, the controller manager should:
- fully exit or roll back the configuration lifecycle transition
- not leave the system in an active/spinning state
- allow tests or processes to terminate normally

**Screenshots**
N/A (logs below)
```
[INFO] Configuring controller: 'bad_chainable_controller'
[ERROR] Controller 'bad_chainable_controller' is chainable, but does not export any state or reference interfaces
(hangs)
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- ROS 2 Version: Rolling
- Workspace: local build of ros2_control
- No modifications to core logic (issue observed while adding test coverage)

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here, especially include any modifications to ros2_control that relate to this issue.

5. Observe that ERROR is returned and logged correctly, however the process/test does not terminate and hangs unless interrupted
Expected: ERROR
Actual: returns ERROR but system does not terminate cleanly
After returning ERROR, the controller manager should:
[ERROR] Controller 'bad_chainable_controller' is chainable, but does not export any state or reference interfaces
I added calls to `cleanup_controller` for both the case where the chainable controller has no interfaces and the case where exporting the interfaces raises an exception.

comments.body:
Hi! I created a PR to attempt to remedy this. The return points in the `configure_controller` function that had to with chainable controllers weren't cleaning up the controller (ie transitioning it back to UNCONFIGURED from INACTIVE) during early returns.

I added calls to `cleanup_controller` for both the case where the chainable controller has no interfaces and the case where exporting the interfaces raises an exception.

title: Zero controller update rate might trigger undefined behavior

fault_phenomenon.title: Zero controller update rate might trigger undefined behavior
fault_phenomenon.description:
https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/bb07fdd55a59ea750f06bb2fee7a3a1c113b10dd/controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp#L1606

If a user creates a controller with update rate equals to zero, the line above is undefined behavior according to the C++ docs. Modulo operator with 0 should not be used. Maybe there should be a check of the controller update rate before using it.

comments.body: This issue is being labeled as stale because it has been open 45 days with no activity. It will be automatically closed after another 45 days without follow-ups.

This actually can never happen because

This parameter is initialized with cm update rate
https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/2296fd89e1b362d56c973709c32b030d98f091fc/controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp#L2480-L2481
and only will be changed if great than zero
https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/2296fd89e1b362d56c973709c32b030d98f091fc/controller_interface/src/controller_interface_base.cpp#L220

But there should maybe added a check here, just to avoid any regression in the future

solution_evidence_candidates.text:
The abort looks like a real out-of-bounds access in `mock_components::GenericSystem` when `calculate_dynamics_` is enabled.

In `hardware_interface/src/mock_components/generic_system.cpp`, the dynamics branch stores state/command in:

- `std::array<double, 3> joint_state_values_` (pos/vel/acc)

…but later mirrors values back using `standard_interfaces_` (pos/vel/acc/effort). If the code iterates up to `standard_interfaces_.size()` (4) while indexing `joint_state_values_` (size 3), `std::array::operator[]` will hit `__n < this->size()` and abort (which matches your Resolute/libstdc++ assert).

On current `master`, this appears to be fixed by iterating up to `joint_state_values_.size()` instead (commit `dee3ca81a`). Cherry-picking that change into whatever branch/PR is running the Resolute CI should turn this into a normal test failure instead of a hard abort.

title: `ros2_control_node` fails to start up on Windows/RoboStack in Jazzy or newer

fault_phenomenon.title: `ros2_control_node` fails to start up on Windows/RoboStack in Jazzy or newer
fault_phenomenon.description:
**Describe the bug**
On RoboStack + Pixi + Windows, `ros2_control_node` crashes in Jazzy and newer.

**To Reproduce**
Make a simple Pixi environment in Windows with this as your `pixi.toml`.

```toml
[workspace]
channels = ["conda-forge", "https://prefix.dev/robostack-jazzy"]
platforms = ["win-64"]

[dependencies]
ros-jazzy-ros-base = "*"
ros-jazzy-controller-manager = "*"
```

Then, run `pixi shell` and `ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node`.

You get this:

```
(roboplan-ros) PS C:\test> ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node
[INFO] [1784861884.280229500] [controller_manager]: Using Steady (Monotonic) clock for triggering controller manager cycles.
[INFO] [1784861884.287362000] [controller_manager]: Subscribing to '/robot_description' topic for robot description.
[ros2run]: Process exited with failure 3221225477
```

**Expected behavior**
Swap out Jazzy for Humble and you get correct behavior.

```
(roboplan-ros) PS C:\test> ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node
[WARN] [1784862048.093321600] [controller_manager]: 'update_rate' parameter not set, using default value.
[INFO] [1784862048.093449300] [controller_manager]: Subscribing to '~/robot_description' topic for robot description file.
Realtime kernel detection is not supported on Windows.
[INFO] [1784862048.094867600] [controller_manager]: update rate is 100 Hz
[INFO] [1784862048.094932100] [controller_manager]: Spawning controller_manager RT thread with scheduler priority: 50
[WARN] [1784862048.095075200] [controller_manager]: Could not enable FIFO RT scheduling policy: with error number <0>(No error). See [https://control.ros.org/master/doc/ros2_control/controller_manager/doc/userdoc.html] for details on how to enable realtime scheduling.

# at this point, the node is running...
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows
 - Version: Jazzy
 - Pixi + RoboStack

**Additional context**

I don't know what it might be... but given where this line appears, my first guess would be it has to do with the `realtime_tools` stuff, since we don't even get to the print statement about realtime kernel not being supported on Windows.

https://github.com/ros-controls/realtime_tools/blob/0e0bca049675fa6da1579d4fc4d83b10a564b9ab/realtime_tools/src/realtime_helpers.cpp#L52

called by

https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/4bcce091c25d1412bb52261479fd57607a93c021/controller_manager/src/ros2_control_node.cpp#L63

... that or the instantiation of controller manager right above: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/4bcce091c25d1412bb52261479fd57607a93c021/controller_manager/src/ros2_control_node.cpp#L58-L59

Whoa, thanks everyone for the lightning fast investigation!

@christophfroehlich how were you able to tell where this crash occurred? Did you end up having to source build? I guess this would explain all the small related PRs linked to this issue.

The patch of pal_statistics is merged and bloom is also triggered :)
Thanks to all

title: GenericSystem rejects controller reference interfaces when calculate_dynamics is enabled

fault_phenomenon.title: GenericSystem rejects controller reference interfaces when calculate_dynamics is enabled
fault_phenomenon.description:
## **Describe the bug**

When using two `JointTrajectoryController` instances chained to one `PidController`, controller activation fails with `mock_components/GenericSystem` when `calculate_dynamics` is enabled.

The controller chain is:

```text
arm_group_controller     ─┐
                           ├──> pid_controller ───> GenericSystem
gripper_group_controller ─┘
```

The first JTC can be activated, but the second JTC fails. Swapping the startup order changes which JTC fails.

The same configuration works with `gazebo_ros2_control/GazeboSystem`.

### ros2_controllers.yaml

```yaml
controller_manager:
  ros__parameters:
    update_rate: 100

    joint_state_broadcaster:
      type: joint_state_broadcaster/JointStateBroadcaster

    pid_controller:
      type: pid_controller/PidController

    arm_group_controller:
      type: joint_trajectory_controller/JointTrajectoryController

    gripper_group_controller:
      type: joint_trajectory_controller/JointTrajectoryController


pid_controller:
  ros__parameters:
    dof_names:
      - joint1
      - joint2

    reference_and_state_dof_names:
      - joint1
      - joint2

    command_interface: velocity

    reference_and_state_interfaces:
      - position

    use_external_measured_states: false

    gains:
      joint1:
        p: 1.0
        i: 0.0
        d: 0.0

      joint2:
        p: 1.0
        i: 0.0
        d: 0.0


arm_group_controller:
  ros__parameters:
    joints:
      - joint1

    command_joints:
      - pid_controller/joint1

    command_interfaces:
      - position

    state_interfaces:
      - position

    state_publish_rate: 50.0
    action_monitor_rate: 20.0
    allow_partial_joints_goal: false
    open_loop_control: false


gripper_group_controller:
  ros__parameters:
    joints:
      - joint2

    command_joints:
      - pid_controller/joint2

    command_interfaces:
      - position

    state_interfaces:
      - position

    state_publish_rate: 50.0
    action_monitor_rate: 20.0
    allow_partial_joints_goal: false
    open_loop_control: false
```

### rrbot.urdf.xacro

This uses the standard RRBot model from `ros2_control_demo_description`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>

<robot
  xmlns:xacro="http://www.ros.org/wiki/xacro"
  name="rrbot_pid_jtc_poc">

  <xacro:include
    filename="$(find ros2_control_demo_description)/rrbot/urdf/rrbot_description.urdf.xacro"/>

  <xacro:include
    filename="$(find ros2_control_demo_description)/rrbot/urdf/rrbot.materials.xacro"/>

  <link name="world"/>

  <xacro:rrbot parent="world" prefix="">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </xacro:rrbot>

  <ros2_control name="RRBotPIDJTC" type="system">
    <hardware>
      <plugin>mock_components/GenericSystem</plugin>
      <param name="calculate_dynamics">true</param>
    </hardware>

    <joint name="joint1">
      <command_interface name="velocity"/>
      <state_interface name="position">
        <param name="initial_value">0.0</param>
      </state_interface>
    </joint>

    <joint name="joint2">
      <command_interface name="velocity"/>
      <state_interface name="position">
        <param name="initial_value">0.0</param>
      </state_interface>
    </joint>
  </ros2_control>
</robot>
```

## **To Reproduce**

1. Start `controller_manager` with the RRBot description and controller configuration:

   ```bash
   ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
     --ros-args \
     -p robot_description:="$(xacro rrbot.urdf.xacro)" \
     --params-file ros2_controllers.yaml
   ```

2. In another terminal, start the controllers in this order:

   ```bash
   ros2 run controller_manager spawner joint_state_broadcaster \
     -c /controller_manager

   ros2 run controller_manager spawner pid_controller \
     -c /controller_manager

   ros2 run controller_manager spawner arm_group_controller \
     -c /controller_manager

   ros2 run controller_manager spawner gripper_group_controller \
     -c /controller_manager
   ```

3. Inspect the controller and hardware interface states:

   ```bash
   ros2 control list_controllers
   ros2 control list_hardware_interfaces
   ros2 control view_controller_chains
   ```

4. The first JTC is activated successfully.

5. The second JTC fails during activation with an error similar to:

   ```text
   [mock_generic_system]: Joint 'joint2' has to have
   'position', 'velocity', or 'acceleration' interface!

   [resource_manager]: Component 'RRBotPIDJTC' did not accept
   command interfaces combination
   ```

6. If the JTC startup order is swapped, the other JTC fails instead.

## **Expected behavior**

Both JTC controllers should activate successfully:

```text
joint_state_broadcaster    active
pid_controller              active
arm_group_controller        active
gripper_group_controller    active
```

The hardware command interfaces should remain:

```text
joint1/velocity
joint2/velocity
```

The controller reference interfaces should be accepted independently:

```text
pid_controller/joint1/position
pid_controller/joint2/position
```

## **Screenshots**

Not applicable. The failure is demonstrated by the controller manager log output.

## **Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- ROS 2 version: Humble
- `ros2_control`: built from source
- `ros2_controllers`: built from source
- Hardware plugin: `mock_components/GenericSystem`
- Controller chain:
  - Two `JointTrajectoryController` instances
  - One `PidController`
- `calculate_dynamics`: enabled
- The same configuration works with `gazebo_ros2_control/GazeboSystem`

## **Additional context**

The hardware exports:

```text
joint1/velocity
joint2/velocity
joint1/position
joint2/position
```

The PID controller exports the following reference interfaces:

```text
pid_controller/joint1/position
pid_controller/joint2/position
```

The failure occurs only when:

```xml
<param name="calculate_dynamics">true</param>
```

is enabled. With `calculate_dynamics=false`, `GenericSystem::prepare_command_mode_switch()` returns early and the controllers activate.

The relevant implementation in `GenericSystem` uses substring matching:

```cpp
auto joint_it_found = std::find_if(
  info_.joints.begin(), info_.joints.end(),
  [key](const auto & joint)
  {
    return (key.find(joint.name) != std::string::npos);
  });
```

This associates:

```text
pid_controller/joint2/position
```

with the hardware joint:

```text
joint2
```

The implementation then checks whether the full key equals one of:

```text
joint2/position
joint2/velocity
joint2/acceleration
```

and reports an error because the controller reference interface is not a hardware control-mode interface.

`GazeboSystem` does not show this failure because it only handles exact hardware interface names and ignores the controller reference interfaces.

A potential fix is to make `GenericSystem::prepare_command_mode_switch()` and `perform_command_mode_switch()` match only exact hardware interface names, for example:

```cpp
return (
  key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_POSITION ||
  key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_VELOCITY ||
  key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_ACCELERATION);
```

This prevents controller reference interfaces from being interpreted as hardware joint interfaces.

## P.S.

Content generated by agent, but verified and reproduced by human. 
Below patch fixes the thing. 
```diff
diff --git a/hardware_interface/src/mock_components/generic_system.cpp b/hardware_interface/src/mock_components/generic_system.cpp
index b216c708..1632f2d6 100644
--- a/hardware_interface/src/mock_components/generic_system.cpp
+++ b/hardware_interface/src/mock_components/generic_system.cpp
@@ -389,10 +389,19 @@ return_type GenericSystem::prepare_command_mode_switch(
 
   for (const auto & key : start_interfaces)
   {
-    // check if interface is joint
+    // Only handle interfaces owned by this hardware component. Controller
+    // reference interfaces (for example
+    // "pid_controller/joint_name/position") are also present in the command
+    // interface switch request, but must not select a hardware control mode.
     auto joint_it_found = std::find_if(
       info_.joints.begin(), info_.joints.end(),
-      [key](const auto & joint) { return (key.find(joint.name) != std::string::npos); });
+      [key](const auto & joint)
+      {
+        return (
+          key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_POSITION ||
+          key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_VELOCITY ||
+          key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_ACCELERATION);
+      });
 
     if (joint_it_found != info_.joints.end())
     {
@@ -478,10 +487,17 @@ return_type GenericSystem::perform_command_mode_switch(
 
   for (const auto & key : start_interfaces)
   {
-    // check if interface is joint
+    // Ignore controller reference interfaces and handle only exact hardware
+    // interface names.
     auto joint_it_found = std::find_if(
       info_.joints.begin(), info_.joints.end(),
-      [key](const auto & joint) { return (key.find(joint.name) != std::string::npos); });
+      [key](const auto & joint)
+      {
+        return (
+          key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_POSITION ||
+          key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_VELOCITY ||
+          key == joint.name + "/" + hardware_interface::HW_IF_ACCELERATION);
+      });
 
     if (joint_it_found != info_.joints.end())
     {
```

title: Data race on overruns.print_warnings during diagnostic parameter refresh

fault_phenomenon.title: Data race on overruns.print_warnings during diagnostic parameter refresh
fault_phenomenon.description:
**Describe the bug**

Diagnostics assign `*params_ = cm_param_listener_->get_params()` while the real-time loop reads `params_->overruns.print_warnings`.

- Write: [controller_manager.cpp:4439](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/ffcf444a69a5bdae7b19d09fc7e45e0224386231/controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp#L4439), `controller_activity_diagnostic_callback()`.
- Read: [controller_manager.cpp:3679](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/ffcf444a69a5bdae7b19d09fc7e45e0224386231/controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp#L3679), `write()`.

The diagnostic callback holds the controller-list mutex, but `write()` reads the flag without that mutex. Updating the snapshot therefore races with the read.

**To Reproduce**

Requires ROS 2 Lyrical, colcon, rosdep, Clang 18.

Build the affected revision in a ROS workspace:

```bash
source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash
mkdir -p ~/ros2_control_tsan_ws/src
cd ~/ros2_control_tsan_ws
git clone https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control.git src/ros2_control
git -C src/ros2_control checkout ffcf444a69a5bdae7b19d09fc7e45e0224386231
rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -r -y
colcon build --packages-up-to controller_manager --cmake-args \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++-18 \
  '-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-fsanitize=thread -g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer --gcc-install-dir=/usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/15' \
  -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS=-fsanitize=thread \
  -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS=-fsanitize=thread
```

Terminal 1:

```bash
cd ~/ros2_control_tsan_ws
source install/setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=181
export TSAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=0:external_symbolizer_path=/usr/bin/llvm-symbolizer-18'
ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node --ros-args \
  -p update_rate:=1000 -p diagnostic_updater.period:=0.001 \
  -p overruns.print_warnings:=false
```

Terminal 2, after Terminal 1 reports that it is waiting for the robot description:

```bash
cd ~/ros2_control_tsan_ws
source install/setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=181
robot_description='<robot name="tsan_repro">
  <link name="base"/><link name="tip"/>
  <joint name="joint1" type="revolute">
    <parent link="base"/><child link="tip"/>
    <limit lower="-1" upper="1" effort="1" velocity="1"/>
  </joint>
  <ros2_control name="TestSystem" type="system">
    <hardware><plugin>mock_components/GenericSystem</plugin></hardware>
    <joint name="joint1">
      <command_interface name="position"/><state_interface name="position"/>
    </joint>
  </ros2_control>
</robot>'
ros2 topic pub --once --qos-durability transient_local \
  /robot_description std_msgs/msg/String "{data: '$robot_description'}"
```

Once Terminal 1 reports `Resource Manager has been successfully initialized`, run in Terminal 2:

```bash
for i in {1..50}; do
  ros2 param set /controller_manager overruns.print_warnings true
  ros2 param set /controller_manager overruns.print_warnings false
done
```

Terminal 1 can report a one-byte TSan race between `Params::operator=()` in the diagnostic callback and `ControllerManager::write()`. Repeat the loop if needed.

**Expected behavior**

Runtime changes to `overruns.print_warnings` should take effect without racing with the real-time loop.

**Screenshots**

Not applicable.

**Environment**

- Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64; ROS 2 Lyrical.
- ros2_control 6.9.0, commit `ffcf444a69a5bdae7b19d09fc7e45e0224386231`.
- Clang 18 ThreadSanitizer .

**Additional context**

Observed TSan stack excerpt on the unmodified revision above:

```text
Write of size 1:
  Params::operator=(Params&&)
  ControllerManager::controller_activity_diagnostic_callback()
    controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp:4439
Previous read of size 1:
  ControllerManager::write()
    controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp:3679
```

**Proposed fix**

Add `#include <atomic>` and a member in `controller_manager.hpp`:

```cpp
std::atomic<bool> overruns_print_warnings_{true};
```

Initialize the cache in `initialize_parameters()` and update it after each parameter snapshot refresh in `set_initial_hardware_components_state()`, `controller_activity_diagnostic_callback()`, and `hardware_components_diagnostic_callback()`:

```cpp
overruns_print_warnings_.store(params_->overruns.print_warnings, std::memory_order_relaxed);
```

In `ControllerManager::write()`, replace the read of `params_->overruns.print_warnings` with:

```cpp
overruns_print_warnings_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)
```

This preserves runtime updates and avoids a blocking lock in the real-time loop. Relaxed ordering is sufficient for this independent flag. The change will covers this flag only and modifies two files (`+9/-1`).

## Bug report

**Required Info:**

- Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04
- ROS2 Version: Foxy
#### Steps to reproduce issue
Set goal pose to a position the robot can not reach. For example close the door after the robot entered the room and than set the goal pose outside the room. 
**Edit:** 
To reproduce it with TB3 I started my turtlebot3_world with: `ros2 launch turtlebot3_gazebo turtlebot3_world.launch.py`. Than start slam_toolbox async mode: `ros2 launch slam_toolbox online_async_launch.py`. 
Start nav2 navigation: `ros2 launch nav2_bringup navigation_launch.py`. 
Start rviz2, drive the turtlebot around to get a full map. Stop next to any wall. Set the Goal Pose outside of the "Arena" and it slowly turns into the wall until it hits it. 
All parameters were set default and I used the apt install not the source for the prove with turtlebot.
The turtlebot is much slower hitting the wall than the real robot. The real robot hits it pretty fast. I think because it doesnt slow down fast enough. Setting the inflation radius higher should help, so at least it slows down earlier shouldnt it?

The robot searches for a path to get to the point and stops with an error message when it can't reach the goal.

I use an omnidirectional robot platform with one laserscanner in front (180 degrees) and the Intel T265 camera as odometry signal. While this test slam_toolbox was running in online_async mode.

error_logs.text: The robot searches for a path to get to the point and stops with an error message when it can't reach the goal.

https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/1823 fixed a recovery node error because of which the main child of the recovery node was not retried after executing the second child. Before this patch, the flow of the recovery node was:

code_and_log_blocks.text:
<RecoveryNode number_of_retries="2" name="ComputePathToPose">
    <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
    <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Context" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
</RecoveryNode>

<RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="ComputePathToPose">
    <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
    <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Context" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
</RecoveryNode>

solution_evidence_candidates.text:
> Where was this originally introduced?

https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/1823 fixed a recovery node error because of which the main child of the recovery node was not retried after executing the second child. Before this patch, the flow of the recovery node was:
first child (fails) -> second child (succeeds) -> recovery node (succeeds)

After this path, the flow of the recovery node was changed to:
first child (fails) -> second child (succeeds) -> first child (succeeds) -> recovery node (succeeds)

>  I don't see how the commit hash you linked to could cause that issue (since N has been > 1 I believe always).

The number of retries for the planner specific recovery node has always been 1 because of which this issue was masked before https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/1823
https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/a30816f2939e441f2054df0f40775adb76b57997/nav2_bt_navigator/behavior_trees/navigate_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml#L11

I don't think the clear costmap service returns a timeout, the service executes correctly and ends up clearing the costmap. I think this issue is caused because of the time it takes to rebuild the costmap after it has been cleared. The planner server calls `getPlan()` right after the clear costmap service executes which makes me think that the planner actually ends up planning on the cleared costmap before the sensor data is received and the costmap is rebuilt again.

The timeout I added just before `getPlan()` is called gives the costmap enough time to receive sensor data and rebuild its layers after which the planner is able to plan correctly. This should confirm that the planner ends up planning on an empty costmap if it's called right after the clear costmap service executes and returns success.

comments.body: Please reformat your ticket and provide specific reproduction instructions in the TB3 default world (and any parameter changes from default you had to make to have this occur).

With turtlebot its all still default. 
On the real robot, the major changes should be in the DWB Controller the velocities and accelerations. Furthermore the robot has a rectengular footprint and not a radius like the turtlebot. 
Like mentioned in the edit: The turtlebot slows down but keeps moving and than hits the wall (see the gif I added) 
I think setting a bigger inflation radius in my real setup should slow down the process because the robot slows down earlier. Do I understand this right? But is it the expected behavior that the path gets planned through a wall?

I don't see any attempt at planning into that space from your gif, I just see a robot driving into a wall which is inside of the minimim range of the laser. It wouldn't surprise me if the laser gazebo plugin doesn't properly handle collision objects there resulting in that little nub in the map. But I don't see any action items here. 

I can't reproduce any replanning outside of valid space in the default TB3 world without doing really unreasonable things trying to get it to do so like spawning inside walls or putting it in an impossible position.

Cannot get it to display nice on github, but hope this video makes this issue clearer
[![Play Video here](https://streamable.com/e/degbst)](https://streamable.com/e/degbst)

This is super strange, I was just testing on my branch working on Hybrid-A* and I don't see this at all, but current main branch does, thanks for bringing this up. So something's changed letting this happen from after Jun 17.

It looks like the bug was introduced in e850db02ba88e03e2b6519e2b2ad51bbdc9f97f6 after the fix in `RecoveryNode` logic. I reverted this patch and everything seems to work as expected but that only happens because `RecoveryNode` doesn't retry `ComputePathToPose` again after it fails the first time and the planner specific recovery is called (which is what this patch was supposed to fix).

Even after reverting e850db02ba88e03e2b6519e2b2ad51bbdc9f97f6,  this bug can still be reproduced by increasing the number of retries in the planning branch to anything > 1:

```xml
<RecoveryNode number_of_retries="2" name="ComputePathToPose">
    <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
    <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Context" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
</RecoveryNode>
```

So I figured out the actual reason behind this bug.

Currently, when you give a goal when there's no valid path to the goal the first `ComputePathToPose` call will fail since the planner is not able to plan a valid path. The `RecoveryNode` then calls `ClearEntireCostmap` and clears the global costmap. In the very next iteration within a fraction of a second `RecoveryNode` retries `ComputePathToPose` and this time the planner plans on an empty global costmap since the global costmap was cleared and hasn't spawned back up yet. The planner is able to find a straight path to the invalid goal, `ComputePathToPose` succeeds and we have the bug!!

I added a 1 second sleep just above this line to test this and it checks out, everything works as expected:
https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/506384f2bcf32978428278f65567bfaf429d6d63/nav2_planner/src/planner_server.cpp#L238

Where was this originally introduced? Was it from a BT update to include clearing costmaps as a failure action in planning? I don't see how the commit hash you linked to could cause that issue (since N has been > 1 I believe always). 

I see the server_timeout for clear costmaps is 10ms https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/f237751f557b2e921e08f96d4749bfe3f2b2b091/nav2_bt_navigator/src/bt_navigator.cpp#L126 and looking at the service caller https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/main/nav2_behavior_tree/include/nav2_behavior_tree/bt_service_node.hpp#L102 we shouldn't be returning from the service node until after its completed the clear costmaps action.

So I'd be curious what the return code from `check_future` is. If its timeout, we just need to increase that timeout, if its success, then there's something wrong in costmap_2d because we should not be returning from the service until things are good again. It wouldn't surprise me at all if this was actually another DDS issue and services were failing again and its manifesting for us in this way because its timing out mid-execution. 

If that was the case, that sleep you added would have the same effect because the service call was received by costmap but not finished, so then when the planner is planning, the clearing is still underway causing that overlap. If that is indeed what's happening (not that the timeout isn't big enough, but service calls are failing), then we really need a better way to identify that situation or get around it if this will be an issue that comes up over and over again.

But its not clear to me where this got introduced.

> Where was this originally introduced?

https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/1823 fixed a recovery node error because of which the main child of the recovery node was not retried after executing the second child. Before this patch, the flow of the recovery node was:
first child (fails) -> second child (succeeds) -> recovery node (succeeds)

After this path, the flow of the recovery node was changed to:
first child (fails) -> second child (succeeds) -> first child (succeeds) -> recovery node (succeeds)

>  I don't see how the commit hash you linked to could cause that issue (since N has been > 1 I believe always).

The number of retries for the planner specific recovery node has always been 1 because of which this issue was masked before https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/1823
https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/blob/a30816f2939e441f2054df0f40775adb76b57997/nav2_bt_navigator/behavior_trees/navigate_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml#L11

I don't think the clear costmap service returns a timeout, the service executes correctly and ends up clearing the costmap. I think this issue is caused because of the time it takes to rebuild the costmap after it has been cleared. The planner server calls `getPlan()` right after the clear costmap service executes which makes me think that the planner actually ends up planning on the cleared costmap before the sensor data is received and the costmap is rebuilt again.

The timeout I added just before `getPlan()` is called gives the costmap enough time to receive sensor data and rebuild its layers after which the planner is able to plan correctly. This should confirm that the planner ends up planning on an empty costmap if it's called right after the clear costmap service executes and returns success.

> After this path, the flow of the recovery node was changed to:
> first child (fails) -> second child (succeeds) -> first child (succeeds) -> recovery node (succeeds)

For  the recovery node, I don't think that's good behavior, I think the original was correct. If the planner is now passing, we shouldn't be triggering the clear costmap again. Imagine this recovery was backing up or something, we'd be backing up, in a good state, and then backing up again.

> The timeout I added just before getPlan() is called gives the costmap enough time to receive sensor data and rebuild its layers after which the planner is able to plan correctly. This should confirm that the planner ends up planning on an empty costmap if it's called right after the clear costmap service executes and returns success.

I would just make sure its not timing out, because that's something we can more easily do something about. If it really just needs time, that becomes more complicated to deal with. We'd need to keep flags between clears and updates so that we can wait until the costmap is valid again to use.

> If the planner is now passing, we shouldn't be triggering the clear costmap again. Imagine this recovery was backing up or something, we'd be backing up, in a good state, and then backing up again.

I think you misinterpreted my comment. The `RecoveryNode` is the parent node which triggers its second child when the first child fails. The second child is assumed to be the recovery behavior that you want to execute when your main execution branch (`RecoveryNode`'s first child) fails. Taking the planning branch as an example:

```xml
<RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="ComputePathToPose">
    <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"/>
    <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap-Context" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
</RecoveryNode>
```

Before #1823, the `RecoveryNode` would have returned success right after `ClearEntireCostmap` returns success without re-ticking `ComputePathToPose`. The flow in that case would be:
ComputePathToPose (fails) -> ClearEntireCostmap (succeeds)
At this point, `RecoveryNode` just returns success without going back to `ComputePathToPose`. This is also why the planning through walls issue never showed up before #1823.

After #1823, the flow becomes:
ComputePathToPose (fails) -> ClearEntireCostmap (succeeds) -> ComputePathToPose (succeeds)
The first child of `RecoveryNode` is executed again after a successful recovery (second child) executes. At this point `RecoveryNode` returns success. This should be the expected behavior right?

> I would just make sure its not timing out, because that's something we can more easily do something about.

I checked the return code from the `ClearEntireCostmap` service, it returns success. 100% sure now that it's the planner planning on an empty costmap issue.

> This should be the expected behavior right?

That does sound right I misread ` recovery node (succeeds)` part - I thought that was meaning the recovery behavior action. God, the nomenclature we used in this is going to be messing with my head for years to come, isn't it? 

> I checked the return code from the ClearEntireCostmap service, it returns success. 100% sure now that it's the planner planning on an empty costmap issue.

Ok. 

My knee-jerk solution would be to add a variable to `Costmap2DROS` about whether it was cleared, and if so, it needs to wait for a new update before planning. Or in the clear costmap services themselves, the last step is an `update` for the costmap so that by the time it returns, it already did a sync.
@pfedom @naiveHobo please review / test this patch in https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/2044

@SteveMacenski I'm getting similar behavior at regular intervals. I thought that this patch could fix that, but unfortunately, it doesn't help at all. The main difference is that I'm not using amcl, but the map and localization is provided by SLAM at 1 Hz. The rest of the configuration is the same. By any chance, these are related? fault_phenomenon.description:
## Bug report

- Operating System:
  - Ubuntu 22.04
 - ROS2 Version:
  - Humble Source

After the binary packages sync on 18.08.2023 the `nav2_mppi_controller` started crashing on when launching;
![image](https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/assets/49076784/dd23ff38-5843-4ead-8f35-b4d06e519e19)

ps: same non-updated setup still working.

By the way, the sync was supposed to fix this issue but it hasn't been solved yet: https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/issues/3762#issuecomment-1684283651

error_logs.text: This is another issue. Please compile with debug flags according to the docs here (https://navigation.ros.org/tutorials/docs/get_backtrace.html) and give me the traceback to know where the crash is occurring. I looked over the recent changes and I can't find anything obvious that would cause this. Make sure that you clean build (e.g. delete install/build spaces) in case there's some caching issue causing this from a major sync update
What is your computer architecture? That is also not a traceback, that doesn't show me where the issue is in particular. I still don't see anything obviously wrong to address.

I compiled from source `1.1.9` tag, and it is working, but the binaries still give the error I mentioned above. I also tried it on many different computer architectures but still, binaries throw an error and crash.
Then after the preferforwardcritic loaded .The error occur:

`[ERROR] [controller_server-15]: process has died [pid 13909, exit code -4, cmd '/opt/ros/humble/lib/nav2_controller/controller_server --ros-args --log-level info --ros-args -r _ --params-file /tmp/tmpsaf6nhx7 -r /tf:=tf -r /tf_static:=tf_static -r cmd_vel:=cmd_vel_nav'].`

That error is notably different from the others! Can you check where that happens. The 2 dynamic casts I see are
If you disinclude the obstacle critic, are there any other traceback points that show up now? This seems like progress. If we update the layer cast to

You should never be crashing from source builds on the same CPU as it was compiled on. If that's what's happening, then that's totally unrelated to any of this and lets discuss that separately. If its from moving `libs` around, that dynamic cast error is new from the errors we had before and oddly its called **before** the previous crash location so we should have seen it before?

I'm hoping that's your issue... Otherwise that's just issue one of potentially others. May be worth at that time on your local builds using the `no-avx512` flag so that we have that part of the problem squared away and start looking at this last remaining one. I can say though that I'm not sure I've ever seen that error you mention
[ERROR] [1696005038.942448416] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Caught exception in callback for transition 10
[ERROR] [1696005038.942551782] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Original error: basic_string::_M_create
[WARN] [1696005038.942729878] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Error occurred while doing error handling.
[FATAL] [1696005038.942828285] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Lifecycle node controller_server does not have error state implemented
However, if I run with the local build workspace being sourced instead and with the obstacles critic enabled, I do not get the segfault crashes, but I do get the same error as above.
> However, if I run with the local build workspace being sourced instead and with the obstacles critic enabled, I do not get the segfault crashes, but I do get the same error as above.

Then, I went commit by commit. When all is built from 0cf04629 (`1.1.9`), there are no problems when copying individual libs. When all is re-built from commit 0ca14fe0, and then I copy just the MPPI libs to `/opt/ros/humble/lib/` and run, I get the `dynamic_cast` segfault with the MPPI obstacle critic, and the `basic_string::_M_create` error without the obstacle critic. So at this point, I think the MPPI libs are probably expecting to use something that was added in 0ca14fe0 to a dependency package, which is not in my install since I copied only the MPPI files and nothing else.
/opt/ros/humble/lib/nav2_controller/controller_server: symbol lookup error: /opt/ros/humble/lib/libnav2_costmap_2d_core.so: undefined symbol: _ZN9nav2_util13LifecycleNode18on_rcl_preshutdownEv
/opt/ros/humble/lib/nav2_controller/controller_server: symbol lookup error: /opt/ros/humble/lib/libcontroller_server_core.so: undefined symbol: _ZN9nav2_util13LifecycleNode18on_rcl_preshutdownEv
[ERROR] [1696413455.157859635] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Caught exception in callback for transition 10
[ERROR] [1696413455.157900562] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Original error: std::bad_alloc
[WARN] [1696413455.157958950] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Error occurred while doing error handling.
[FATAL] [1696413455.157998690] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Lifecycle node planner_server does not have error state implemented

All of this is resulting from just copying individual lib files around. The error I was getting when running from an environment that has the nav2 workspace sourced were in fact because I have the config set so that all of the available controller plugins get loaded at startup (`controller_plugins: ["FollowPathDWB", "FollowPathTEB", "FollowPathRPP", "FollowPathMPPI"]`). And the error was coming from TEB not MPPI as I initially thought:
[ERROR] [1696414607.282713391] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Caught exception in callback for transition 10
[ERROR] [1696414607.282806769] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Original error: std::bad_alloc
[WARN] [1696414607.282867601] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Error occurred while doing error handling.
[FATAL] [1696414607.282911811] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Lifecycle node controller_server does not have error state implemented
- ` And the error was coming from TEB` LOL, classic TEB

The error from TEB looks to be of the same nature as mixing of old and new lib versions. I re-compiled the whole nav2 workspace from `1.1.11`. And I quickly tried re-compiling all of TEB with the `1.1.11` nav2 workspace being sourced (so it would use the new libraries during compilation and not the old ones) and it seems to have solved the problem. So from what I see, it might be necessary for people to re-compile TEB after the newer nav2 release is downloaded and that should solve the issues if they appear.

>I have an intel i7-8565U and 1.1.9 is broken for me. I also see this problem on my Intel CPU using the libs you provided me with optimize not included (and obviously included). Which did you build those libs on, Intel or AMD? It also may not be simply as easy as AMD->Intel but also the relative age. Have something older than an 11th gen to test on?

I was hoping a bit that it could be that simple. But all the libs I sent you were built with `AMD Ryzen 7 3700X` and they are clearly still failing for you. It would be interesting to see which exact instructions it is failing at in this case, since my AMD certainly does not show any `avx512` variant in the supported flags (see https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/issues/3767#issuecomment-1729821852). And if both cases (with or without `optimize`) still fail in the same way, there is probably still something else going on. I do have an older `i5 7600K` that I can test this with once I get to that PC.

>Supposedly also the build farm is using AMD for building the binaries https://build.ros2.org/job/Hbin_uJ64__nav2_mppi_controller__ubuntu_jammy_amd64__binary/11/consoleFull

I couldn't find any reference to the specific HW being used. The `amd64` tag should only specify the 64-bit architecture name (regardless of Intel or AMD). What I also find strange is that the release libs that I have downloaded from the build farm still fail at the same `avx512` instructions, which would be strange if they were compiled on AMD without `avx512`.  However I may be overreaching my knowledge here, and it might be possible that the instruction set is in fact supported on some AMD CPUs as well.

>Does it work for you on your NUC if you take the binaries from the build farm and from the AMD processor with optimize on? That's an interesting datapoint.

Yes, they all work. I was not able to get it NOT working with any test.

>Actually, just pull in Humble again after https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/pull/3836 is merged. This includes those changes I made to MPPI. You can just use that instead to test if my changes fixed some or all of these issues

So rebuilding the MPPI package individually either way does not produce any changes unless it is rebuilt together with the other dependencies.

Then, I went commit by commit. When all is built from 0cf04629 (`1.1.9`), there are no problems when copying individual libs. There's alot of good stuff here, so I want to parrot back to you the highlights to make sure we're on the same page
- You completely clean rebuilt from 1.1.9 and things worked as expected -- so something in your workflow in moving the libs around it compiling was causing some of the issues 
- Adding the `mno-avx512f` at this point solved the problems with portability 
- The process of moving libs around with older stuff is causing the issue that you're currently facing. While I looked at https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/0ca14fe0db48d98ecbb71365073bb2ae811df240 and see nothing obvious to why that could crash, that could be an ABI compability thing that us mere mortals looking at code cannot figure out without going much deeper into analysis. But I don't think that's called for in this case since its a test workflow issue, not an issue intrinsic to the problem we're solving
- ` And the error was coming from TEB` LOL, classic TEB

> I'm not sure if this behavior is even an issue since it is expected that when a dependency to a package changes and the package is ported individually without it's changed dependency it is going to cause problem

Agreed. 

> However, shouldn't minor revisions still be cross-portable independently?

No, only within a distribution compatibility is assured. Rolling / main is bleeding edge so anything can change anytime. You shouldn't generally expect to be able to take a package from version X and apply it to the stack at version Y off mainline. In a released distro (e.g. humble, iron, etc) you should be able to do that.

---

So in summary here: it sounds like its all fixed and if I bloom up a new release, we should be good to go on this issue in entirety. I think you mention some other TEB problem, but its unclear to me if that's an issue from the version X package and version Y framework or something else that should be addressed

Releases cut! The issue should be resolved next humble / iron sync!

still follow up on TEB if there’s anything actionable!

> You completely clean rebuilt from 1.1.9 and things worked as expected

Yes.

> Adding the mno-avx512f at this point solved the problems with portability

Yes.

> The process of moving libs around with older stuff is causing the issue that you're currently facing.

Yes, If I start mixing old `1.1.9` packages with the newer versions then there are issues.  And when I completely re-build `1.1.11` and don't copy any individual lib files but instead source the whole nav2 workspace and use that, it also worked. But only if TEB was excluded at that point.

> that could be an ABI compability thing

Yes, it does seem like something of that nature to me.  It might be due to the way some of the libraries are linked to each other during compilation and a change in one core part manifests across multiple other ones. But I'm just speculating here. It basically required most of the nav2 packages to be on the same updated versions and not just some to make it work.

> So in summary here: it sounds like its all fixed and if I bloom up a new release, we should be good to go on this issue in entirety.

Yes, I believe so. When all (or almost all) packages are at the same release version, and there are no mixtures of old `1.1.9` and newer like `1.1.11`, I wouldn't (hopefully) expect any issues.

> still follow up on TEB if there’s anything actionable!

The error from TEB looks to be of the same nature as mixing of old and new lib versions. I re-compiled the whole nav2 workspace from `1.1.11`. And I quickly tried re-compiling all of TEB with the `1.1.11` nav2 workspace being sourced (so it would use the new libraries during compilation and not the old ones) and it seems to have solved the problem. So from what I see, it might be necessary for people to re-compile TEB after the newer nav2 release is downloaded and that should solve the issues if they appear.

```
And it's the same thing when I install form the `1.1.11` deb file. Are the deb packages `iron` or `humble`?

Regarding the local `humble` builds, I am transferring the locally compiled lib files to `/op/ros/humble/lib/` and running with `/opt/ros/humble` as the source path. And It's the same behavior as with the deb installs.

However, if I run with the local build workspace being sourced instead and with the obstacles critic enabled, I do not get the segfault crashes, but I do get the same error as above.

I'll try building again from the `1.1.9` tag prior to the fixes, where I didn't have these new issues (omitting the obvious `avx512` thing that started this whole conversation) and see if there's anything different on my side there. I'll also try messing with the `mtune` flag.

> May be worth at that time on your local builds using the no-avx512 flag so that we have that part of the problem squared away and start looking at this last remaining one.

I'll do that when I get to the NUC.

I can't currently explain why these new errors started happening now, they weren't a problem previously. But a small pattern I see is that they started only happening from versions related to `1.1.10` and `1.1.11`.

> sudo apt install ./ros-humble-nav2-mppi-controller_1.1.10-1jammy.20230927.201948_amd64.deb --reinstall

Standard is more `dpkg -i` for local binaries but my guess is that's what this is doing anyway. But in the off case its different, worth a try. I don't know if `apt install --reinstall` tries to do something fancy. I doubt it, but good to point out just in case.

> And it's the same thing when I install form the 1.1.11 deb file. Are the deb packages iron or humble?

Humble

> However, if I run with the local build workspace being sourced instead and with the obstacles critic enabled, I do not get the segfault crashes, but I do get the same error as above.

I think that points to a problem in your workflow if the built workspace transferring libs and taking debians of the same thing don't result in the same outcomes.

> I'll try building again from the 1.1.9 tag prior to the fixes, where I didn't have these new issues (omitting the obvious avx512 thing that started this whole conversation) and see if there's anything different on my side there. I'll also try messing with the mtune flag.

OK! The different from .9 to .10 are these three commits https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/b0a68bb5ef7df8ae3347358f8e453a688d423a55 https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/91b688de212036d2c33b15437652dff156a4ff66 https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/1b13476dc91d9bde130506c03332e39e4d2d9aac

.10 to .11 adds https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/2d6e9a96354c0ea763e70eedd81225635f7b9db5 only 

Hopefully those should be easy to test anything meaningful that's changed. You may also benefit from enacting a clean restart of your previous changes to make sure you haven't landed up in an odd state -- unless it is really just `-mtune=generic`. But I'm surprised it works fine for me if it doesn't work on your Intel machines given that mine is substantially older. 

Edit: I did some research on `mtune` and `generic` is what is set when `march=native`. As long as march isn't set to an exact processor name, `mtune=generic` shouldn't actually change anything. Still worth a shot, but I'm thinking increasingly it might be stale / odd state on your end. Can someone else (@MichalMalachowski @AmmarAlbakri ) also test this on their AMD or newer Intel computers to get a 3rd opinion? I don't want to poo-poo you if this is actually just a "my computer is the odd man out" situation and everyone else is still having issues.

> Standard is more dpkg -i for local binaries but my guess is that's what this is doing anyway.

Yes, at least from my understanding, the `apt install` should just invoke `dpkg -i` behind the scenes either way (if you give it a local path to deb it will use that instead of searching on remote) and the `--reinstall` option is there to make sure it didn't skip the installation if it found that the package is already installed. I tried with `dpkg -i` as well and there's no difference.

> I think that points to a problem in your workflow if the built workspace transferring libs and taking debians of the same thing don't result in the same outcomes.

If I'm manually copying the locally compiled libs to `/opt/ros/humble/lib/` it is producing exactly the same behavior as installing from the debians. The different behavior is only when I source the nav2 workspace instead of having `/op/ros/humble/` sourced.

I checked-out at the `1.1.9` tag and first tried re-building only the `nav2_mppi_controller` package (using `--packages-select`) with all else still left at https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/b3474caa7a316dda00b30e265aa71e3c0f3bb355 (this means it should use the already compiled dependencies during the compilation of MPPI). That did not make a difference - I was still getting the same errors.

Then I completely cleaned the build and install space and re-built the whole nav2 from `1.1.9`.  And here it did work without any problems. Either copying libs, or sourcing the nav2 workspace, all of it worked without errors. At this point I tried setting and unsetting the `mtune=generic` flag and that does not make a difference, so that is not a problem.

While at this working state, I checked the `mno-avx512f` flag by setting it together with `march=native` explicitly, and building on the `Intel i7-1165G7` CPU:
```
add_compile_options(-O3 -finline-limit=10000000 -ffp-contract=fast -ffast-math -march=native -mno-avx512f)
target_link_libraries(${lib} xtensor xtensor::optimize xtensor::use_xsimd)
```
When ported to an AMD PC, the libs worked without problems. If the `mno-avx512f` flag was removed it crashed at the illegal instruction. If it was added, it worked OK. So, from my end, I can also confirm that this problem should be resolved.

Regarding the new errors I've been getting, it seems they don't relate to changes in `nav2_mppi_controller` but changes in the other dependency packages instead, when the libs are moved around individually. When I re-build only `nav2_mppi_controller` from the newest 6e35cc7417463c3f441c0d7fc596cff251cdfe4b commit (`--packages-select`) and left all else still at `1.1.9`, it did not break anything and all still worked fine. So rebuilding the MPPI package individually either way does not produce any changes unless it is rebuilt together with the other dependencies.

Then, I went commit by commit. When all is built from 0cf04629 (`1.1.9`), there are no problems when copying individual libs. When all is re-built from commit 0ca14fe0, and then I copy just the MPPI libs to `/opt/ros/humble/lib/` and run, I get the `dynamic_cast` segfault with the MPPI obstacle critic, and the `basic_string::_M_create` error without the obstacle critic. So at this point, I think the MPPI libs are probably expecting to use something that was added in 0ca14fe0 to a dependency package, which is not in my install since I copied only the MPPI files and nothing else.

Going from the MPPI dependencies listed in `CMakeLists.txt`, when I start porting those libs one by one (all compiled from 0ca14fe0) some of them now expect to find the added pre-shutdown callback methods.
* When `nav2_planner` or `nav2_lifecycle_manager` are ported to `/op/ros/humble/`, it doesn't make any difference.
* When `nav2_costmap_2d` lib is ported to `/opt/ros/humble/`: 
```
/opt/ros/humble/lib/nav2_controller/controller_server: symbol lookup error: /opt/ros/humble/lib/libnav2_costmap_2d_core.so: undefined symbol: _ZN9nav2_util13LifecycleNode18on_rcl_preshutdownEv
```
* When `nav2_controller` lib is ported to `/op/ros/humble/`:
```
/opt/ros/humble/lib/nav2_controller/controller_server: symbol lookup error: /opt/ros/humble/lib/libcontroller_server_core.so: undefined symbol: _ZN9nav2_util13LifecycleNode18on_rcl_preshutdownEv
```
* When I then also port `nav2_util`, which defines the added pre-shutdown methods errors start popping up from planners:
```
[INFO] [1696413455.157573423] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Created global planner plugin GridBasedNavFn of type nav2_navfn_planner/NavfnPlanner
[INFO] [1696413455.157816263] [NavfnPlanner]: Destroying plugin GridBasedNavFn of type NavfnPlanner
[ERROR] [1696413455.157859635] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Caught exception in callback for transition 10
[ERROR] [1696413455.157900562] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Original error: std::bad_alloc
[WARN] [1696413455.157958950] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Error occurred while doing error handling.
[FATAL] [1696413455.157998690] [loki_sim.planner_server]: Lifecycle node planner_server does not have error state implemented
```
All of this is resulting from just copying individual lib files around. The error I was getting when running from an environment that has the nav2 workspace sourced were in fact because I have the config set so that all of the available controller plugins get loaded at startup (`controller_plugins: ["FollowPathDWB", "FollowPathTEB", "FollowPathRPP", "FollowPathMPPI"]`). And the error was coming from TEB not MPPI as I initially thought:
```
[INFO] [1696414607.072932515] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Created controller : FollowPathTEB of type teb_local_planner::TebLocalPlannerROS
[INFO] [1696414607.093805826] [TEBLocalPlanner]: Footprint model 'circular' (radius: 0.220000m) loaded for trajectory optimization.
[INFO] [1696414607.093885236] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Parallel planning in distinctive topologies enabled.
[ERROR] [1696414607.282713391] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Caught exception in callback for transition 10
[ERROR] [1696414607.282806769] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Original error: std::bad_alloc
[WARN] [1696414607.282867601] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Error occurred while doing error handling.
[FATAL] [1696414607.282911811] [loki_sim.controller_server]: Lifecycle node controller_server does not have error state implemented
```
When I remove TEB from the config and run from the environment that has the nav2 workspace sourced, I have no errors and all works. So here, all of the re-compiled packages from 0ca14fe0 are within the sourced environment path and it all works. If I make similar experiments with this environment - first building all of nav2 from `1.1.9` and then re-building only individual packages from 0ca14fe0 instead of rebuilding all (`--packages-select nav2_mppi_controller nav2_util`) - I get the same behavior. I also went through the individual changes, and the errors start once the `rcl_preshutdown_cb_handle_` and the accompanying methods are added in `nav2_util -> lifecycle_node.hpp` and `nav2_util -> lifecycle_node.cpp`.

A pattern I would deduce from this would be that the added pre-shutdown in 0ca14fe0 made a lot of the older pre- 0ca14fe0 binaries incompatible with the new ones? So after this change, compatibility with TEB is also broken? That would explain why I started getting the errors when I install the newer MPPI libs from the debians or port the newer libs compiled locally. I'm not sure if this behavior is even an issue since it is expected that when a dependency to a package changes and the package is ported individually without it's changed dependency it is going to cause problems. However, shouldn't minor revisions still be cross-portable independently? So this would mean that if I update my `nav2_mppi_controller` from `1.1.9` to say `1.1.10`, but leave all of the other packages still at `1.1.9` it would break (which is what happens when I do an install from the debians).

This was always my nav2 building environment:
```
ROS_VERSION=2
ROS_PYTHON_VERSION=3
AMENT_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/ros/humble
PYTHONPATH=/opt/ros/humble/lib/python3.10/site-packages:/opt/ros/humble/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages
LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gazebo-11/plugins:/opt/ros/humble/opt/rviz_ogre_vendor/lib:/opt/ros/humble/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/opt/ros/humble/lib
ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=0
PATH=/home/ubuntu//.local/bin:/opt/ros/humble/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/snap/bin
ROS_DISTRO=humble
```
So it should be just the native ros install with no additional workspaces.

There's alot of good stuff here, so I want to parrot back to you the highlights to make sure we're on the same page
- You completely clean rebuilt from 1.1.9 and things worked as expected -- so something in your workflow in moving the libs around it compiling was causing some of the issues 
- Adding the `mno-avx512f` at this point solved the problems with portability 
- The process of moving libs around with older stuff is causing the issue that you're currently facing. While I looked at https://github.com/ros-planning/navigation2/commit/0ca14fe0db48d98ecbb71365073bb2ae811df240 and see nothing obvious to why that could crash, that could be an ABI compability thing that us mere mortals looking at code cannot figure out without going much deeper into analysis. But I don't think that's called for in this case since its a test workflow issue, not an issue intrinsic to the problem we're solving
- ` And the error was coming from TEB` LOL, classic TEB

> I'm not sure if this behavior is even an issue since it is expected that when a dependency to a package changes and the package is ported individually without it's changed dependency it is going to cause problem

Agreed. 

> However, shouldn't minor revisions still be cross-portable independently?

No, only within a distribution compatibility is assured. Rolling / main is bleeding edge so anything can change anytime. You shouldn't generally expect to be able to take a package from version X and apply it to the stack at version Y off mainline. In a released distro (e.g. humble, iron, etc) you should be able to do that.

---

So in summary here: it sounds like its all fixed and if I bloom up a new release, we should be good to go on this issue in entirety. I think you mention some other TEB problem, but its unclear to me if that's an issue from the version X package and version Y framework or something else that should be addressed

Releases cut! The issue should be resolved next humble / iron sync!

still follow up on TEB if there’s anything actionable!

> You completely clean rebuilt from 1.1.9 and things worked as expected

Yes.

> Adding the mno-avx512f at this point solved the problems with portability

Yes.

> The process of moving libs around with older stuff is causing the issue that you're currently facing.

Yes, If I start mixing old `1.1.9` packages with the newer versions then there are issues.  And when I completely re-build `1.1.11` and don't copy any individual lib files but instead source the whole nav2 workspace and use that, it also worked. But only if TEB was excluded at that point.

> that could be an ABI compability thing

Yes, it does seem like something of that nature to me.  It might be due to the way some of the libraries are linked to each other during compilation and a change in one core part manifests across multiple other ones. But I'm just speculating here. It basically required most of the nav2 packages to be on the same updated versions and not just some to make it work.

> So in summary here: it sounds like its all fixed and if I bloom up a new release, we should be good to go on this issue in entirety.

Yes, I believe so. When all (or almost all) packages are at the same release version, and there are no mixtures of old `1.1.9` and newer like `1.1.11`, I wouldn't (hopefully) expect any issues.

> still follow up on TEB if there’s anything actionable!

The error from TEB looks to be of the same nature as mixing of old and new lib versions. I re-compiled the whole nav2 workspace from `1.1.11`. And I quickly tried re-compiling all of TEB with the `1.1.11` nav2 workspace being sourced (so it would use the new libraries during compilation and not the old ones) and it seems to have solved the problem. So from what I see, it might be necessary for people to re-compile TEB after the newer nav2 release is downloaded and that should solve the issues if they appear.
